doc:
Biology 2023 Ordinary Level, deferred sitting: reviewed task ledger, carded for the first time.

Independent visual sweep (2026-11-19), every page rendered and read:
  * LC025GLP038EV (deferredexams/2023; Sections A and B and Answerbook), 40 pages: p1 cover, p2
    instructions, p3-p8 Section A Questions 1-7, p9-p11 Section B Questions 8-10, p12 Section C
    answerbook instructions, p13-p14 graph paper, p15-p39 ruled answer pages, p40 back cover with the
    copyright notice.
  * LC025GLP040EV (Section C), 12 pages: p1 cover, p2-p10 Questions 11-17, p11 "Do not hand this
    question paper up", p12 back cover with the copyright notice.
  * LC025GLP000EV (deferredmarkingschemes/2023), 24 pages: p1 cover, p2 the deferred-scheme note, p3
    introduction, p4-p5 marking examples, p6 the annotations table, p7 the Irish-medium bonus table,
    p8-p22 Questions 1-17, p23 "BLANK PAGE", p24 back cover.

The sitting has the June 2023 Ordinary shape (any five of Section A, any two of B, any four of C). The
deferred scheme sets out every printed ask, so no card needs the "prints no answer" row. Every part is
laddered as printed (Q1, Q3 2(7) + 3(2); Q2, Q4-Q7 8 + 7 + 5(1); Section B (a) 5 + 1 and (b) 2(9) +
6(1); Section C 5 + 2(2), 3(5) + 6(2), 2(6) + 6(2); Q16/Q17 2(7) + 8(2)): every response is carded at its
ladder's first rate and counted against the part's "Number of correct responses" table (CHECKSUMS).
Q2's ticks are read from their positions. Three choice asks whose options the scheme answers
differently are ROUTES (Q4(d) arthritis or osteoporosis; Q5(e) Parkinson's disease or paralysis;
Q10(b)(iv) a starch plate with iodine or a milk plate with biuret). Numbered asks (Q11(b)(iv)1-2,
Q11(b)(v)1-2, Q12(b)(vii)1-2, Q13(c)(ii)1-2, Q13(c)(vi)1-2, Q16(a)(iii)1-2, Q16(a)(v)1-2,
Q16(b)(iii)1-3, Q17(a)(iii)1-2, Q17(d)(iv)1-2, Q17(d)(v)1-2) are separately counted responses, carded
one each. Underlined terms (Q13(a)(i), Q15(b)(iv)) are shown on crops of the printed question; Q17(b)(iv)
shows the printed table to complete and carries the scheme's completed table as its solution figure.
SELECTION_SCAN: Instructions: "blue or black pen", not a question.
Section A rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section B rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section C rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Q2 "true or false": the answer options.
Q3 "Choose each term": a matching list, every term placed; one card per lettered description.
Q6(b)(i) "any two gases": both required on the scheme's two rows; one card.

Q7(e) "both animals and plants": description, not a choice.
Q9(b)(iv) "product (or products)": one answer; one card.
Q9(b)(vii) "Label both axes": both required; one card.
Q10(b) "either starch or skimmed milk": the scheme answers (iv) for each plate type: ROUTES.
Q10(b)(iii) "in both plates": one reagent for both; one card.
Q10(b) figure note "Both plates were flooded with test reagent": printed matter.
Q11(a): every term asked, one card each.
Q11(b)(ii) "stated in the article or otherwise": source of the answer, not a choice of task.
Q11(b)(iii) "from the passage or otherwise": source of the answer, not a choice of task.
Q11(b)(iv)2 "any one of the following areas": open choice of area; one card.

Q11(c)(iv) "any one of the animals": open single answer; one card.
Q12(a): every term asked, one card each.
Q12(c)(vi) "in either plants or animals": open single answer; one card.

Q13(c)(ii) "each of the following stages": each stage asked, one card per item.

Q14(c)(v) "any one useful substance": open single answer; one card.
Q15(a)(ii) "any two adaptations": bounded menu; one card.
Q15(b)(v) "either monocotyledonous or dicotyledonous": description, both terms asked; one card.
Q15(c)(iii) "any one example": open single answer; one card.
Q16 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q16(d)(vii) "any one cause": open single answer; one card.
Q16(d)(vii) "any one corrective measure": open single answer, same card.
Q17 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q17(a)(vi) "any two components": bounded menu; one card.
Q17(b)(ii) "any two other types": bounded menu; one card.
Q17(b)(iii) "any two methods": bounded menu; one card.
Q17(b)(iv) "the following table": a reference; every cell asked; one card.
Q17(d)(ii) "any two of these organs": bounded menu; one card.

q4-joint: Diagram of a free moving joint in section: two bone ends meet inside a capsule; A points to the band at the side of the joint, B to the smooth layer covering a bone end, C to the space between the bone ends, and a box with the letter X stands beside the upper bone.
q5-neuron: Diagram of a neuron: a cell body with a nucleus and many short branches, A pointing to one of the short branches, and a long fibre with rounded segments along it, B pointing to the fibre; an empty box sits below the fibre.
q6-leaf: Drawing of a leaf with its Petiole and a Vein labelled, and an enlarged section of the leaf beside it with a Stoma labelled on its lower surface.
q7-food-web: Food web drawn with arrows: Grass at the base, eaten by Hare, Insect and Snail; Insect eaten by Frog and Mouse; Snail eaten by Thrush; Frog and Mouse eaten by Fox and Hawk; Thrush eaten by Hawk; Hare eaten by Fox.
q9-graph: Graph with a single peaked curve, its vertical axis labelled by an empty box A and its horizontal axis by an empty box B.
q10-plates: Two agar plates, A and B, each with halved seeds lying on it and labelled Seed; the note between them reads Both plates were flooded with test reagent. In plate A the agar is dark right up to the seeds; in plate B there are clear patches around the seeds.
q13a-question: The printed question: (a) Plants are autotrophic organisms, with autotrophic underlined, then (i) Explain the underlined term.
q13-chloroplast: Diagram of an oval organelle with a double outer membrane and stacks of discs inside.
q14-breathing: Diagram of the human breathing system: the windpipe with Rings of cartilage, branching airways in two lungs, the Rib cage with Intercostal muscle, and the Diaphragm below; A points to one of the two large tubes branching from the windpipe and B to the tiny sacs at the ends of the airways.
q14-urinary: Diagram of the human urinary system: two kidneys with the Renal artery and Renal vein, one kidney cut open showing the Cortex and Renal pelvis; the parts numbered 1 (the tube leading down from a kidney), 2 (the bag at the bottom), 3 (the tube leaving the bag) and 4 (the inner region of the cut kidney).
q15-seed: Diagram of the internal structure of a broad bean seed opened out: B points to one of the two large halves, A to the small structure lying between the halves at the top, and C to the thin outer covering.
q15b-iv-question: The printed question: (iv) The broad bean seed is an example of a non-endospermic seed, with non-endospermic underlined. Explain the underlined term.
q16-root: Diagram of a cross section of a plant part: a round section with a dense central core and many long hairs growing out from its edge; Ground tissue is labelled inside and X points to the outer layer of cells.
q16-villus: Diagram of a villus in section: a finger-shaped projection with a network of vessels, A pointing to the network and B to the central vessel inside it.
q16-rhizopus: Drawing of Rhizopus: upright stalks rising from a horizontal thread, each ending in a round head; A points to a dark round head and B to the branched threads at the base.
q16-male: Diagram of the human male reproductive system in side view: A points to the penis region, B to a gland below the bladder, C to the oval organ in the scrotum, and D to a gland behind the bladder.
q17-circulation: Diagram of the two-circuit circulatory system: the lungs at the top and the body below, joined to the heart by vessels with arrows showing the direction of blood flow; A points to a large vein entering the heart and B to a large artery leaving it.
q17-layering: Drawing of a plant whose stem is bent down and pegged into the soil, where new roots grow from it.
q17b-iv-question: The printed table to copy and complete: columns Reproduction by seed and Reproduction by vegetative propagation; rows Type of reproduction (seed: Sexual), Amount of genetic variation and Approximate duration, the other cells empty.
q17b-iv-scheme: The marking scheme\u2019s completed table: Type of reproduction, Sexual and Asexual; Amount of genetic variation, High and None; Approximate duration, Long and Short.
q17-bacterium: Diagram of a rod-shaped bacterium: X points to the coiled material inside the cell, Y to the outer layers of the cell, and Z to the long whip-like structure at one end.
q17-immune: Outline of a human body with several small organs drawn inside it: in the neck, the chest, the abdomen and the groin.
